backend.measure: sum of the image's unpacked layer sizes (docker history), in MB (10^6 bytes)
backend.justification: Re-measured in P12 when LangGraph joined the runtime dependencies (ADR 021): about 336 MB unpacked, about 106 MB compressed (docker save | gzip). Roughly 148 MB is the Debian and Python base image and the rest the locked production virtual environment. P12 added about 59 MB: langgraph and its checkpoint, prebuilt and sdk packages, langchain-core, langsmith (installed as a langchain-core dependency; tracing stays off because no LANGSMITH variable is ever set), and their native helpers (orjson, ormsgpack, xxhash, zstandard, uuid-utils), plus precompiled bytecode for all of it because the runtime filesystem is read-only. Before that: the AWS SDK about 26 MB (P10), SQLAlchemy 23 MB, cryptography 16 MB, asyncpg 11 MB, pypdfium2 about 6 MB (P9). Earlier baselines: 229 MB (2026-09-21), 277 MB (P10). The application code, migrations and alembic.ini are under 1 MB. The ceiling is the baseline plus 20%: enough for ordinary dependency patch updates, tight enough to catch accidental bloat such as a forgotten cache, a dev dependency or a copied directory. Deliberately not optimised further. The test refuses a ceiling more than 25% above the recorded baseline.

frontend.measure: sum of the image's unpacked layer sizes (docker history), in MB (10^6 bytes)
frontend.justification: First clean build of frontend/Dockerfile on nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.31.6-alpine3.24: about 59.7 MB unpacked, about 23 MB compressed (docker save | gzip). Almost all of it is the base image: roughly 9 MB Alpine, 6 MB nginx and 44 MB of nginx's own packages and modules. The site itself (the Next.js static export, 0.76 MB) and nginx.conf are under 1 MB, and there is no Node, npm or node_modules in the runtime stage. The ceiling is the baseline plus 20%: enough to absorb a base image patch update, tight enough to catch a leaked build stage (a Node runtime alone would add well over 100 MB) or a copied directory. Deliberately not optimised further. The test refuses a ceiling more than 25% above the recorded baseline.
